etc/fr_os/dhcpcd6.conf.text:
# Managed by FR_OS (frfw.ipv6) -- regenerated on every `apply`, do not edit.
# IPv6 (ROADMAP FND-1): SLAAC from the provider's Router Advertisement,
# DHCPv6 for an address and a delegated prefix on the WAN; a /64 of the
# prefix for each LAN device (FND-1b), with an unreachable route installed
# for the rest of it.
ipv6only
noipv4
noipv4ll
# Router Advertisements are read on the WAN only (its block below): never
# on a LAN, which must not configure the router -- and dhcpcd.conf(5)
# advises it when asking for a delegated prefix.
noipv6rs
# No hostname and no FQDN option: the router doesn't name itself to the
# provider.
fqdn disable
# No hook script: nothing the provider sends is written to the router's
# own files (resolv.conf, its hostname, NTP servers).
script /bin/true
# Stable addresses that don't carry the MAC (RFC 7217).
slaac private
# The LAN devices too: dhcpcd only assigns a prefix to an interface it
# runs on.
allowinterfaces eth0 eth1

interface eth0
	ipv6rs
	ia_na 1
	ia_pd 101 eth1/0/64

etc/fr_os/dnsmasq_adblock.conf.text:
# Managed by FR_OS (frfw.adblock.dns_service) -- regenerated on every
# `apply`, do not edit by hand. A dedicated, frfw-owned dnsmasq
# instance (fr-adblock-dns.service) -- never the system's own
# dnsmasq.service/dnsmasq.conf, which this never touches.
port=53
no-resolv
no-hosts
addn-hosts=@ROOT@/etc/fr_os/adblock.hosts
interface=lo
interface=eth1
# Each address of those interfaces, and the ones they get later (ROADMAP
# FND-1c): IPv6 addresses come and go -- the provider's prefix is
# renumbered, the stable ULA one is added by the next apply.
bind-dynamic
server=1.1.1.1
server=9.9.9.9
user=nobody
group=nogroup
# No PID file: systemd tracks the process, and /run is read-only in the
# unit's sandbox (security-lessons I1). Without this dnsmasq writes
# /run/dnsmasq.pid even in the foreground.
pid-file=

etc/fr_os/dnsmasq_ra.conf.text:
# Managed by FR_OS (frfw.ipv6) -- regenerated on every `apply`, do not edit.
# Router Advertisements on the LAN (ROADMAP FND-1b/1c), and nothing else:
# each device's /64s, for SLAAC -- the one dhcpcd gave it from the
# provider's prefix and the stable ULA one -- and, where the router's
# resolver serves the zone, the resolver's address (RDNSS).

no-hosts

# Managed by FR_OS (frfw.ipv6) -- regenerated on every `apply`, do not edit.
# IPv6 (ROADMAP FND-1): SLAAC from the provider's Router Advertisement,

# for the rest of it.
ipv6only
noipv4
noipv4ll
# Router Advertisements are read on the WAN only (its block below): never
# on a LAN, which must not configure the router -- and dhcpcd.conf(5)
# advises it when asking for a delegated prefix.

script /bin/true

# The LAN devices too: dhcpcd only assigns a prefix to an interface it

interface eth0

etc/fr_os/dnsmasq_adblock.conf.text:
# Managed by FR_OS (frfw.adblock.dns_service) -- regenerated on every
# `apply`, do not edit by hand. A dedicated, frfw-owned dnsmasq
# instance (fr-adblock-dns.service) -- never the system's own
# dnsmasq.service/dnsmasq.conf, which this never touches.
port=53
no-resolv
no-hosts
addn-hosts=@ROOT@/etc/fr_os/adblock.hosts
interface=lo
# Each address of those interfaces, and the ones they get later (ROADMAP
# FND-1c): IPv6 addresses come and go -- the provider's prefix is
# renumbered, the stable ULA one is added by the next apply.
bind-dynamic
server=1.1.1.1
local=/lan/
host-record=nas.lan,192.168.10.20
local=/nas.lan/
address=/intranet.example.com/10.73.1.5
local=/intranet.example.com/
user=nobody
group=nogroup
# No PID file: systemd tracks the process, and /run is read-only in the
# unit's sandbox (security-lessons I1). Without this dnsmasq writes
# /run/dnsmasq.pid even in the foreground.
pid-file=

version: 1
hostname: fr-router
timezone: Europe/Budapest
zones:
  wan: {}
  lan:
    description: LAN
  iot: {}
  vpn: {}
interfaces:
  wan:
    device: eth0
    zone: wan

  dst_port: 22
- name: lan-out
  action: accept
  from_zone: lan
  to_zone: wan
- name: night
  action: drop
  from_zone: iot
  to_zone: wan
  schedule:
    days:
    - weekdays
    start: '22:00'
    end: 06:00
- name: temp
  action: accept
  from_zone: lan
  to_zone: wan
  proto: tcp
  dst_port: 8000-8100
  expires: ' 2026-12-01T18:00 '

  action: drop
  from_zone: lan
  to_zone: wan
  src_address:
  - 10.73.1.5/32
  - 2001:db8:5::/48
nat:
  masquerade:
  - out_zone: wan
  port_forwards:
  - name: web
    in_zone: wan
    proto: tcp
    dst_port: 8443
    to_address: 10.73.1.10
    to_port: 443
dhcp:
  lan:
    range_start: 10.73.1.100
    range_end: 10.73.1.199
    dns_servers:
    - 10.73.1.1
    reservations:
    - mac: AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:01
      address: 10.73.1.50
      hostname: nas
adblocker:
  enabled: true
  source_urls:
  - https://example.org/hosts
  serve_lan: true
  allowlist:
  - example.com
  categories:
    social:
    - https://example.org/social
app_control:
  enabled: true
  blocked_apps:
  - tiktok
local_dns:
  domain: lan
  hosts:
    nas.lan: 10.73.1.50
  overrides:
    printer.home.arpa: 10.73.1.60
xdp_sni_filter:
  enabled: true
  interfaces:
  - lan
  blocklist:
  - bad.example
tls_fingerprint:
  enabled: true
  blocklist:
  - t13d1516h2_8daaf6152771_e5627efa2ab1
  - fingerprint: '00000000000000000000000000000000'
    label: x
iot:
  enabled: true
  zones:
  - iot
  trusted_macs:
  - aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:02
ai_ids:
  enabled: true
  excluded_macs:
  - aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:03
ztna:
  enabled: true
  users:
  - username: kolos
    password_hash: pbkdf2$x
update:
  repo: starsmash29/FR_OS-pblk
metrics:
  site: budapest-office
  token_sha256: aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa
management:
  zones:
  - lan
  addresses:
  - 10.73.1.1
wireguard:
  enabled: true
  address: 10.99.0.1/24
  endpoint: vpn.example.org
  peers:
  - name: phone
    public_key: AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA=
    address: 10.99.0.2/32
logging:
  drops: true
  drops_per_minute: 20
ipv6:
  enabled: true
  pinholes:
  - name: nas-https
    zone: lan
    host: ::5054:ff:fe12:3456
    proto: tcp
    port: 443

# IPv6 (ROADMAP FND-1): SLAAC from the provider's Router Advertisement,

etc/fr_os/dhcpcd6.conf.text:
# Managed by FR_OS (frfw.ipv6) -- regenerated on every `apply`, do not edit.
# IPv6 (ROADMAP FND-1): SLAAC from the provider's Router Advertisement,
# DHCPv6 for an address and a delegated prefix on the WAN; a /64 of the
# prefix for each LAN device (FND-1b), with an unreachable route installed
# for the rest of it.
ipv6only
noipv4
noipv4ll
# Router Advertisements are read on the WAN only (its block below): never
# on a LAN, which must not configure the router -- and dhcpcd.conf(5)
# advises it when asking for a delegated prefix.
noipv6rs
# No hostname and no FQDN option: the router doesn't name itself to the
# provider.
fqdn disable
# No hook script: nothing the provider sends is written to the router's
# own files (resolv.conf, its hostname, NTP servers).
script /bin/true
# Stable addresses that don't carry the MAC (RFC 7217).
slaac private
# The LAN devices too: dhcpcd only assigns a prefix to an interface it
# runs on.
allowinterfaces eth0 eth1

interface eth0
	ipv6rs
	ia_na 1
	ia_pd 101 eth1/0/64

# Managed by FR_OS (frfw.adblock.dns_service) -- regenerated on every
# `apply`, do not edit by hand. A dedicated, frfw-owned dnsmasq
# instance (fr-adblock-dns.service) -- never the system's own
# dnsmasq.service/dnsmasq.conf, which this never touches.
port=53
no-resolv
no-hosts
addn-hosts=@ROOT@/etc/fr_os/adblock.hosts
interface=lo
interface=eth1
# Each address of those interfaces, and the ones they get later (ROADMAP
# FND-1c): IPv6 addresses come and go -- the provider's prefix is
# renumbered, the stable ULA one is added by the next apply.
bind-dynamic
server=1.1.1.1
server=9.9.9.9
user=nobody
group=nogroup
# No PID file: systemd tracks the process, and /run is read-only in the
# unit's sandbox (security-lessons I1). Without this dnsmasq writes
# /run/dnsmasq.pid even in the foreground.
pid-file=

etc/fr_os/dnsmasq_ra.conf.text:
# Managed by FR_OS (frfw.ipv6) -- regenerated on every `apply`, do not edit.
# Router Advertisements on the LAN (ROADMAP FND-1b/1c), and nothing else:
# each device's /64s, for SLAAC -- the one dhcpcd gave it from the

no-hosts

# Router Advertisements are read on the WAN only (its block below): never

# Managed by FR_OS (frfw.ipv6) -- regenerated on every `apply`, do not edit.
# IPv6 (ROADMAP FND-1): SLAAC from the provider's Router Advertisement,
# DHCPv6 for an address and a delegated prefix on the WAN; a /64 of the
# prefix for each LAN device (FND-1b), with an unreachable route installed
# for the rest of it.
ipv6only
noipv4
noipv4ll
# Router Advertisements are read on the WAN only (its block below): never
# on a LAN, which must not configure the router -- and dhcpcd.conf(5)
# advises it when asking for a delegated prefix.
noipv6rs
# No hostname and no FQDN option: the router doesn't name itself to the
# provider.
fqdn disable
# No hook script: nothing the provider sends is written to the router's
# own files (resolv.conf, its hostname, NTP servers).
script /bin/true
# Stable addresses that don't carry the MAC (RFC 7217).
slaac private
# The LAN devices too: dhcpcd only assigns a prefix to an interface it
# runs on.
allowinterfaces eth0 eth1 eth1.30

interface eth0
	ipv6rs
	ia_na 1
	ia_pd 101 eth1/0/64 eth1.30/1/64

# Managed by FR_OS (frfw.ipv6) -- regenerated on every `apply`, do not edit.
# IPv6 (ROADMAP FND-1): SLAAC from the provider's Router Advertisement,
# DHCPv6 for an address and a delegated prefix on the WAN; a /64 of the
# prefix for each LAN device (FND-1b), with an unreachable route installed
# for the rest of it.

noipv4
noipv4ll
# Router Advertisements are read on the WAN only (its block below): never
# on a LAN, which must not configure the router -- and dhcpcd.conf(5)
# advises it when asking for a delegated prefix.

# No hostname and no FQDN option: the router doesn't name itself to the
# provider.
fqdn disable
# No hook script: nothing the provider sends is written to the router's
# own files (resolv.conf, its hostname, NTP servers).
script /bin/true
# Stable addresses that don't carry the MAC (RFC 7217).
slaac private
# The LAN devices too: dhcpcd only assigns a prefix to an interface it
# runs on.
allowinterfaces eth0 eth1

interface eth0
	ipv6rs
	ia_na 1
	ia_pd 101 eth1/0/64

# Managed by FR_OS (frfw.adblock.dns_service) -- regenerated on every
# `apply`, do not edit by hand. A dedicated, frfw-owned dnsmasq
# instance (fr-adblock-dns.service) -- never the system's own
# dnsmasq.service/dnsmasq.conf, which this never touches.
port=53
no-resolv
no-hosts
addn-hosts=@ROOT@/etc/fr_os/adblock.hosts
interface=lo
interface=eth1
# Each address of those interfaces, and the ones they get later (ROADMAP
# FND-1c): IPv6 addresses come and go -- the provider's prefix is
# renumbered, the stable ULA one is added by the next apply.
bind-dynamic
server=1.1.1.1
server=9.9.9.9
user=nobody
group=nogroup
# No PID file: systemd tracks the process, and /run is read-only in the
# unit's sandbox (security-lessons I1). Without this dnsmasq writes
# /run/dnsmasq.pid even in the foreground.
pid-file=

# Managed by FR_OS (frfw.ipv6) -- regenerated on every `apply`, do not edit.
# Router Advertisements on the LAN (ROADMAP FND-1b/1c), and nothing else:
